items.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: I don’t know if you heard the Dick Hyman set, Dick said, “Look,” he came to us before we played

ctx.x: But those are some kind of complex arrangements but you pull them off pretty easily. Do you play differently with that group?

I don’t know, I try never to play differently. I just try to play. And it either works or it doesn’t. I can temper my style to a certain degree. For example last night, I don’t know if you heard the Dick Hyman set, Dick said, “Look,” he came to us before we played, he said, “let’s take a different approach to this, just play this very loosely and let it go where it goes.” And there’s certainly the structure, you know, we’re playing within the tune. So we’ll go to a certain length but I don’t try and do things…
I mean there’s a fairly ambiguous direction anyway, let’s play this fairly loose?
